minutes.headline: Green Communities task force passed over the October 8 grant round and will aim for the April round.
minutes.summary: The task force weighed filing for the October 8 competitive grant round, mainly for streetlight LED conversion. It concluded there was not enough time to write, advertise and evaluate an RFP, and a motion to pass over October 8 and target April was seconded and approved by voice. They also discussed closing out current projects, the grant consultant's help, the retirement of the school energy contact, and organizing the committee in September.

votes.motion: Pass over the October 8th grant round and concentrate on going forward to the April round.

Consultant's contract, which ends September 30, to be extended to about March 31.

what_happened.line: The task force voted by voice to pass over the October 8 Green Communities grant round and aim for the April round instead.
Members judged there was not enough time to write, advertise and evaluate an RFP before October 8; streetlight LED conversion was the main project considered.
The chair asked for a calendar of benchmarks leading to the April application date, to be assembled at a future meeting.
Closeout of current grant projects is now expected by the end of February rather than September 3.
The consultant's contract, which ends September 30, is to be extended to about March 31, and the chair will seek an early-September in-person meeting to elect officers.

why_it_matters: Streetlight LED conversion, a way to lower the town's electric costs through state grant money, will not be funded from the October round and now depends on an April application.
If a grant project's estimate comes in over, the town would have to cover the difference, so the timing of closeout and of the next RFP bears on what the town budget may be asked to absorb.
